experts.name: Don Norman
experts.grounding: The Design of Everyday Things, rev. ed. 2013 -- signifiers, errors as design failures not user failures
key_contributions: Framed the whole brief around 'a clock affords nothing,' which the page's own CSS comment already uses correctly -- credited the author rather than re-deriving it.
Identified the .q7 colour-overload finding's significance as a broken signifier, not a style nit.
Co-developed R8's grouping proposal.

experts.name: Dieter Rams
experts.grounding: Ten principles for good design (Vitsoe, 1976 talk) -- 'as little design as possible,' 'makes a product understandable'
key_contributions: Proposed collapsing the glossary into a native <details> (R9) as subtraction rather than addition.
Set the ordering condition on R7 (since-last-visit banner must not outrank staleness/rate-limit warnings).
Deferred the second-gauge-grammar idea on the grounds that a new visual vocabulary is a cost even when the CSS itself is cheap.

experts.name: Edward Tufte
experts.grounding: The Visual Display of Quantitative Information, 1983 -- data-ink ratio, chartjunk, graphical integrity/lie factor
key_contributions: Named the four-representations-of-one-fact (countdown, absolute date, gauge, tally) question at the top of the day, held rather than answered immediately.
Diagnosed the gauge's one-shape-two-referents problem (T2's miniature case) as a transfer risk, not a dishonesty risk.
Argued the flat equal-weight tally (line 901) misallocates ink relative to the Constitution's actual weighting -- basis for R8.

experts.name: B.J. Fogg
experts.grounding: 'A Behavior Model for Persuasive Design,' Persuasive 2009 (B=MAT); Tiny Habits, 2019 (B=MAP). Returning voice from ../record-votes-panel/panels/panel-01-critical.md.
key_contributions: Set the hour-one frame: this page can work on ability and prompt, not motivation, which is fixed for this cohort this quarter.
Authored R7 (since-you-were-last-here banner) in full, including its zero-marginal-API-cost argument.
Proposed and then withdrew the mailto/deep-link idea on hitting AGENTS.md's no-personal-data wall -- modeled costing an idea that dies on inspection, per the brief's instruction.

experts.name: George Orwell
experts.grounding: 'Politics and the English Language,' 1946 -- six rules, incl. active voice and short words over long ones
key_contributions: Line-by-line read of the vote block's sentences; found the toleration sentence (lines 923-925) already the best-written on the page and left it unchanged.
Rewrote the Tier C two-denominators sentence into three short sentences (R10).
Surfaced the Tier-C dual-grouping problem (T2) by rereading voteOf()'s own code comment literally rather than only the style block.

experts.name: Jakob Nielsen
experts.grounding: 'How Users Read on the Web,' Alertbox 1997; 'F-Shaped Pattern for Reading Web Content,' Alertbox 2006 (n=232)
key_contributions: Computed the realistic worst-case line count before a reader reaches the critical sentence in a Tier C vote block (up to nine lines), grounding T1.
Scoped Orwell's editing effort to high-traffic sentences only, explicitly declining to polish rarely-seen error text.
Raised the empirical risk in T3 -- that grouping by effect also erases a social distinction (toleration vs. true silence) worth preserving somewhere.

experts.name: Christopher Alexander
experts.grounding: The Timeless Way of Building, 1979 ('the quality without a name'); A Pattern Language, 1977
key_contributions: Entered an explicit standing reservation at hour one about the mechanistic vocabulary, returned to it only once concretely rather than relitigating it all day.
Found the .q7 overload by grepping the whole script rather than trusting the style block alone -- the panel's single most load-bearing piece of due diligence.
Named T2 (the Tier-C dual-grouping problem) as the sharpest tension of the day, superseding T1 in the register's ordering.

cross_panel_continuity.note: Fogg is the only voice shared with ../record-votes-panel/. Justified in thinking/planning.md as continuity on a question he is already on record about, not padding; his contribution here (R7) is new material, not a restatement of the prior panel's findings.
